By default, NATS waits up to 10 seconds for the `nats-server` to send the initial "ready" signal, [1]. To adjust this delay, set the `NATS_STARTUP_DELAY` environment variable to a suitable duration, such as "30s" for 30 seconds [1].

The default delay between reconnect attempts is 2 seconds [1]. The client will retry up to 60 times before it gives up [3].

NATS clients shuffle the server list on reconnect to prevent a _thundering herd_ situation where all clients try to reconnect to the same server immediately, causing a denial of service attack [4]. This shuffling does matter if you only configure one server, as there is no server to shuffle from or to.

NATS clients shuffle the server list on reconnect to prevent a _thundering herd_ situation, where all clients try to reconnect to the same server simultaneously, leading to a denial of service attack [4]. This shuffling does matter if you configure only one server, as there would be no randomization, and all clients would attempt to connect to that single server, potentially overwhelming it [4].

[2] [3]. A client flush actually confirms the server has received the published messages by sending a PING message to the server and waiting for a PONG response. According to [3], the client periodically sends PING messages to the server and waits for a PONG response to ensure the connection is working. When an application calls flush, most libraries will put a PING on the outgoing queue of messages and wait for the server's PONG response before declaring the flush successful. The passage [2] reiterates the use of PING/PONG for flush, stating that even though the client uses PING/PONG for flush, the pings sent this way do not count towards the [max outgoing pings](connecting/pingpong.md).

[3] The JetStream key/value store has a feature you don't usually find in key/value stores: the ability to keep a history of the values associated with a key (rather than just the current value). The depth of the history is specified when the key/value bucket is created, and the default is a history depth of 1 (i.e. no history). The maximum history size is 64, if you need more your use case will be better implemented using the Stream functionality directly (where you can set the max number of messages per subject to any value you want) rather than the KV abstraction.
